title: Coherent optical control of a thousand qubits in a three-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
authors: Yue Li, Yuxiang Huang, Yi Li, Xu Cheng, Zihan Xie, Qingyuan Mei, Chang-Ling Zou, Ya Wang, Xinhua Peng, Yiheng Lin, Jiangfeng Du
abstract: Leading quantum platforms are largely limited to one or two dimensions, whereas three-dimensional Coulomb crystals of trapped ions self-assemble into dense qubit arrays with no rearrangement overhead. Coherent optical control of such crystals has nonetheless been out of reach, because the optical transition couples to nearly all $3N$ collective modes, i.e., a thermally occupied quasi-continuum bath. Here we cool about 3,600 modes of a crystal of over 1,200 ions below single-phonon occupation, using a continuous cooling band that spans more than five octaves in vibrational spectrum, from about 50 kHz to 2.1 MHz. The crystal then serves as a register of optical qubits, allowing global initialization, coherent manipulation and collective detection. We demonstrate ensemble optical coherence of 21.6 milliseconds and reduce the optical-transition frequency uncertainty from 389 Hz for a single ion to 12 Hz for over a thousand ions, approaching the expected projection-noise scaling. Our approach could be extended to even larger crystals with phonon-mediated many-body couplings, opening a route towards entanglement-enhanced precision metrology and three-dimensional quantum simulation, particularly with spatial-shaped illumination for region-resolved collective control.
summary: This paper reports on achieving coherent optical control in a massive, three-dimensional trapped-ion crystal. By employing broadband cooling techniques, the researchers managed the dense spectrum of collective motional modes, enabling the crystal to function as a high-fidelity quantum register. This work significantly advances the feasibility of large-scale quantum simulation and metrology using trapped ions.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving coherent optical control in large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals because the optical transition couples to a quasi-continuum bath of collective motional modes.
main_result: The authors successfully cooled thousands of motional modes near the ground state and demonstrated global coherent control, achieving an ensemble optical coherence time of 21.6 ms and reducing frequency uncertainty significantly towards the projection-noise limit.
method: The research combines advanced cooling techniques (continuous cooling band spanning five octaves using parallel-EIT cooling) with high-precision spectroscopy (RSB/BSB) and coherent manipulation (Rabi oscillations) on a large ion crystal.
model_or_system: The system is a 3D Coulomb crystal of over 1,200 trapped ions. The complexity arises from the dense, quasi-continuous spectrum of $\approx 3N$ collective motional modes, which must be managed for global quantum operations.
key_observables: Ensemble optical coherence time (21.6 ms), frequency uncertainty ($\sigma/2\pi$ reduced from 389 Hz to 12 Hz), and mean phonon occupation ($ ar{n} < 0.3$).
important_parameters: Ion number ($N_{	ext{ion}} \approx 1,265$), cooling bandwidth (50 kHz to 2.1 MHz), and the scaling of spectroscopic uncertainty ($N^{-0.48}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the robustness of the spectral envelope and mode frequencies despite variations in the metastable equilibrium configuration of the crystal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 3D crystal configuration and mode density, the broadband near-ground-state cooling process via sideband spectroscopy, and the scaling of frequency uncertainty with increasing ion number.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental platform, the necessity of broadband cooling to manage the dense mode spectrum, the successful implementation of global coherent control, and the quantitative demonstration of enhanced precision scaling in the large ensemble.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the scalability bottleneck in trapped-ion quantum computing by demonstrating control over a highly complex, many-body motional bath, which is a major frontier in AMO physics.
